title: iOS 26.2 broke Notes as a writing tool
body:
For many years, Notes was a rare example of a free, simple, text-first app. It worked like a digital notebook: perfect for writing, journaling, study notes, long thoughts, lists, and tables — without getting in the way.

Since iOS 26.2, this has changed. With the keyboard open, the permanently visible formatting bar and enlarged top navigation bar reduce the usable text area to just a few lines, even on the largest iPhones. As a result, it is no longer possible to see or edit text as a whole.

This breaks core use cases:
• writing and editing paragraphs
• working with lists and tables
• journaling and daily notes
• long-form thinking and studying

This is not a cosmetic change — it is a functional regression. Notes now prioritizes interface elements over content, turning a writing space into a control panel.

Please bring back an option to hide or collapse UI elements, or add a minimal, distraction-free writing mode. Notes used to be a place for thinking in text. I hope it can be again.

title: Good but some problems
body: It’s very good but there are some bad problems! For example, when I make a document and leave the app, There is a chance that it’s deleted and I have to either restore the document or make it all over again! Another problem is that I can’t restore some deleted documents sometimes, for example I made a document about my life and then I accidentally deleted it. I wanted to restore it back but I can’t! These are the problems that should be fixed! Other than that solid app so good job!
